# Document Length Breakdown: OntoCoDec Constraint Effectiveness

## Summary

OntoCoDec's violation reduction is **consistent across document lengths** (~74–84%), even though longer documents produce more total violations. Constraints are equally effective on complex (longer) documents as on simple (shorter) ones.

---

## 1. SciERC (Qwen3-8B, Zero-Shot)

**Binning**: Tertile split on word count. 551 docs total.

| Bin    | #Docs | Word Range | Avg WC |
|--------|-------|-----------|--------|
| Short  | 196   | 5–19      | 15.2   |
| Medium | 180   | 20–27     | 23.3   |
| Long   | 175   | 28–97     | 35.6   |

### 1.1 Violation Counts (total across docs in bin)

| Bin    | Mode          | ET | RV | DR  | CF | Total | Doc-Viol% |
|--------|---------------|----|----|-----|----|-------|-----------|
| Short  | Unconstrained |  1 |  5 |  57 |  0 |    63 |     25.0% |
| Short  | Constrained   |  0 |  0 |   5 |  5 |    10 |      4.6% |
| Medium | Unconstrained |  6 |  9 | 104 |  0 |   119 |     43.9% |
| Medium | Constrained   |  0 |  0 |   7 | 15 |    22 |     10.0% |
| Long   | Unconstrained |  3 | 10 | 104 |  1 |   118 |     40.0% |
| Long   | Constrained   |  0 |  0 |   4 | 20 |    24 |     12.0% |

### 1.2 F1 (macro-avg over docs)

| Bin    | Mode          | E-F1  | R-F1 | Avg Ent | Avg Rel |
|--------|---------------|-------|------|---------|---------|
| Short  | Unconstrained | 32.4% | 8.9% |     3.2 |     2.1 |
| Short  | Constrained   | 32.4% | 8.9% |     3.2 |     2.1 |
| Medium | Unconstrained | 27.8% | 6.7% |     4.6 |     3.2 |
| Medium | Constrained   | 27.8% | 6.7% |     4.6 |     3.3 |
| Long   | Unconstrained | 29.9% | 7.0% |     5.9 |     4.1 |
| Long   | Constrained   | 30.0% | 7.3% |     5.9 |     4.1 |

### 1.3 Constraint Effect

| Bin    | Uncon Viols | Const Viols | Reduction | Reduction% |
|--------|-------------|-------------|-----------|------------|
| Short  |          63 |          10 |        53 |      84.1% |
| Medium |         119 |          22 |        97 |      81.5% |
| Long   |         118 |          24 |        94 |      79.7% |

---

## 2. DocRED (Qwen3-8B, Zero-Shot)

**Binning**: Tertile split on word count. 998 docs total.

| Bin    | #Docs | Word Range | Avg WC |
|--------|-------|-----------|--------|
| Short  | 336   | 129–160   | 144.8  |
| Medium | 332   | 161–208   | 182.1  |
| Long   | 330   | 209–510   | 274.7  |

### 2.1 Violation Counts (total across docs in bin)

| Bin    | Mode          |  ET |   RV |   DR |  CF | Total | Doc-Viol% |
|--------|---------------|-----|------|------|-----|-------|-----------|
| Short  | Unconstrained | 177 | 1238 | 1021 |   9 |  2445 |     95.5% |
| Short  | Constrained   |   0 |    0 |  495 | 138 |   633 |     69.6% |
| Medium | Unconstrained | 147 | 1742 | 1047 |   5 |  2941 |     96.7% |
| Medium | Constrained   |   0 |    5 |  544 | 180 |   729 |     77.0% |
| Long   | Unconstrained | 176 | 2209 | 1162 |   3 |  3550 |     98.7% |
| Long   | Constrained   |   0 |    0 |  731 | 200 |   931 |     80.7% |

### 2.2 F1 (macro-avg over docs)

| Bin    | Mode          | E-F1  | R-F1 | Avg Ent | Avg Rel |
|--------|---------------|-------|------|---------|---------|
| Short  | Unconstrained | 61.1% | 9.3% |    17.1 |    14.8 |
| Short  | Constrained   | 62.6% | 9.6% |    17.2 |    14.9 |
| Medium | Unconstrained | 59.3% | 7.9% |    20.3 |    17.6 |
| Medium | Constrained   | 60.7% | 8.5% |    20.3 |    17.5 |
| Long   | Unconstrained | 53.9% | 5.6% |    24.1 |    21.0 |
| Long   | Constrained   | 54.8% | 5.8% |    24.0 |    20.5 |

### 2.3 Constraint Effect

| Bin    | Uncon Viols | Const Viols | Reduction | Reduction% |
|--------|-------------|-------------|-----------|------------|
| Short  |        2445 |         633 |      1812 |      74.1% |
| Medium |        2941 |         729 |      2212 |      75.2% |
| Long   |        3550 |         931 |      2619 |      73.8% |

---

## 3. Key Findings

1. **Consistent reduction across lengths**: Violation reduction is 80–84% for SciERC and 74–75% for DocRED, with no significant degradation on longer documents.

2. **Longer docs produce more violations**: In DocRED, long docs average 10.8 violations/doc unconstrained vs 7.3 for short docs. OntoCoDec scales proportionally.

3. **ET and RV fully eliminated**: Grammar-constrained decoding eliminates 100% of entity-type and relation-vocabulary violations across all length bins (both datasets).

4. **Residual DR violations in DocRED**: Domain-range violations remain in constrained mode (495–731 per bin). This is consistent with the known limitation that DocRED's 96 relation types create a larger semantic constraint space.

5. **CF violations trade-off**: In SciERC, constrained mode introduces new CF violations (0→5/15/20 across bins) while eliminating ET/RV. The grammar forces valid types, but sometimes assigns different valid types to the same entity across relations.

6. **F1 preserved or improved**: Constrained decoding does not harm extraction quality. DocRED shows slight E-F1 improvement (+0.9–1.5pp) and R-F1 improvement (+0.2–0.6pp) across all bins. SciERC is essentially unchanged.

7. **Long-doc effectiveness**: The most important finding: long documents (where violations are most prevalent) benefit equally from OntoCoDec. The constraint framework does not degrade with document complexity.

\paragraph{Dual-Factor Quantitative Analysis.}
\label{app:dual-factor}

Figure~\ref{fig:dual-factor-scatter} plots residual DR against the product $\bar{\kappa} \times \text{RV}_{\text{baseline}}$ for model$\times$dataset configurations.
For \emph{calibrated} models (Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B; unconstrained ET${<}$3\% on both datasets), a linear fit yields $y = 0.366x - 0.138$ with $R^2 = 0.99$ ($n{=}4$, $F(1,2) = 198.0$, $p \approx 0.058$).
The near-perfect fit confirms the dual-factor pattern from \S\ref{sec:composition}: residual DR is governed by the product of schema tightness and baseline violation rate.
Mistral-7B (unconstrained ET${=}$7.58\% on DocRED) deviates from this pattern: its residual DR on DocRED (33.21\%) substantially exceeds the linear prediction, confirming that when model calibration is insufficient (ET${>}$5\% on either dataset), residual DR is dominated by entity misclassification rather than constraint-search failure.
This motivates a principled exclusion criterion: models with unconstrained ET${>}$5\% on either dataset fall outside the regime where the tightness$\times$RV product is the primary DR driver.
The two DocRED points (high $\bar{\kappa}{=}0.842$) separate cleanly from the two SciERC points (low $\bar{\kappa}{=}0.333$), and within each dataset the model with higher baseline RV shows higher residual DR.

\paragraph{Core result.}
Full S1 reduces DR from 18.46\% to 10.21\% ($\downarrow$45\%), eliminates ET (2.48\%\,$\to$\,0\%), and near-eliminates RV (29.66\%\,$\to$\,0.03\%; the residual 5 triples arise from partial JSON recovery where the grammar FSM completes a structurally valid but relation-name-truncated triple).

CF increases modestly (0.10\%\,$\to$\,2.57\%), lower than SciERC's 9.90\%.

% exp_ids: phase2_docred_grammar_only
\paragraph{Grammar layer surfaces latent violations.}
Grammar-only constraints eliminate RV and ET but \emph{increase} DR from 18.46\% to 26.17\% ($+$42\%).
This counter-intuitive result has a structural explanation: the unconstrained baseline's 29.66\% OOV relation triples cannot be evaluated for DR (no schema entry exists); grammar enforcement assigns these triples valid relation names whose domain/range rules the associated entity types frequently violate.
The grammar layer thus \emph{reveals} latent type incompatibilities, directly motivating the semantic layer.

% exp_ids: phase2_docred_semantic_only, phase2_docred_full_s1
\paragraph{Enabling dependency.}
Semantic-only constraints reduce DR by only 25\% (18.46\%\,$\to$\,13.84\%) while failing to eliminate RV (29.87\%) or ET (4.22\%).
Full S1 achieves a further 26\% relative reduction over semantic-only (13.84\%\,$\to$\,10.21\%), replicating the enabling dependency from SciERC: without grammar-enforced vocabulary, the semantic layer encounters OOV relation types for which no domain/range rules exist.

% exp_ids: phase2_docred_full_s1, llama_docred_full_s1
\paragraph{Zero-shot F1 context.}
Zero-shot R-F1 values (6--8\%) reflect zero-shot RE difficulty; supervised SOTA achieves 49--53\% on SciERC~\citep{zhong2021frustratingly}.
F1 serves primarily as a control variable verifying constraint enforcement preserves extraction quality, not as an optimization target.

\paragraph{Constraint tightness governs enforcement ceiling.}
The residual DR on DocRED (10.21\%) exceeds SciERC (0.93\%) due to per-relation \emph{constraint tightness}: DocRED relations average 5.68 valid type pairs ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.842$) vs.\ 24 on SciERC ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.333$).
Tighter constraints produce narrower grammar$\cap$semantic mask intersections, increasing fallback frequency. The aggregate fallback rate (10.2\%; 1{,}770/17{,}341 triples) closely tracks residual DR (10.21\%), confirming a near-bijection between fallback events and residual violations.

This dual-factor pattern (tightness $\times$ baseline RV) is consistent with cross-dataset and cross-model DR reduction differences.
We omit S2 on DocRED because S1 already achieves near-complete RV/ET elimination and the two-pass overhead is less justified when residual DR is dominated by fallback events rather than forward coreference.

\begin{abstract}
We present \textsc{OntoCoDec}, which compiles Information Extraction (IE) ontology schemas into two composable token-level decoding constraints that provide formal guarantees during autoregressive generation:
(1)~a \emph{grammar layer} (XGrammar context-free grammar) guaranteeing JSON structural validity and entity/relation vocabulary membership (virtually eliminating entity type and relation vocabulary violations); and
(2)~a \emph{semantic layer} guaranteeing per-triple domain/range type compliance via a stateful entity registry and dynamic logit masking.
The two layers compose via bitwise AND on logit masks, with the grammar layer as an enabling prerequisite.
%
Without constraints, Large Language Model (LLM) based IE produces systematic domain/range (DR) violations: 15.37\% on SciERC (7 relations) and 18.46\% on DocRED (96 relations), comparable rates governed by \emph{constraint tightness} rather than ontology scale.
\textsc{OntoCoDec} reduces DR by 42--99\% across three model families (Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B) with no significant F1 cost.
For the primary model (Qwen3-8B): SciERC $+$0.13\,pp ($p{=}0.58$), DocRED $+$0.50\,pp ($p{<}0.001$); other models show comparable or larger gains (\S\ref{sec:cross-model}).
% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_full_s1, phase2_docred_full_s1, llama_docred_full_s1, mistral_docred
For calibrated models, residual DR correlates with the product of schema tightness and baseline violation rate, suggesting that constraint effectiveness is predictable from schema and model characteristics.
Composed with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning, DR reaches $\leq$\,0.09\% (SciERC) and 0.20\% (DocRED) with R-F1 within $\pm$0.6\,pp, confirming orthogonal composability.
Per-relation independent enforcement introduces a cross-field consistency (CF) vs.\ DR trade-off: CF violations arise (up to 12\% in zero-shot) as the cost of per-slot domain/range guarantees; fine-tuning resolves this tension (CF\,$\leq$\,1.2\%).
\end{abstract}

OntoCoDec compiles IE ontology schemas into composable token-level decoding constraints, achieving 42--99\% DR reduction across three models and two datasets with no significant F1 cost.
Composed with LoRA fine-tuning, it reaches DR\,$\leq$\,0.20\% at $<$0.6\,pp F1 cost, confirming orthogonal error targeting.

This pattern has an informative boundary condition: Mistral achieves RV\,=\,0\% on SciERC yet retains DR\,=\,13.4\%, because its dominant error mode is entity type misclassification rather than vocabulary confusion---a factor not captured by the dual-factor product.
We present this as a descriptive characterization with explicit scope rather than a universal predictive law.

CF impact is model-dependent: S1 introduces CF for well-calibrated models (up to 12.02\%) but reduces it for poorly-calibrated ones (Mistral: 56.87\%\,$\to$\,1.27\%).
Ablation confirms CF$\leftrightarrow$DR tension ($+$13.85\,pp; Appendix~\ref{app:cf-dr-tradeoff}); fine-tuning reduces CF by 88\% (\S\ref{sec:composability}); global entity-level type consensus offers the most direct path forward.
